paper_title: Depth Two Majority Circuits for Majority and List Expanders
statement: The existence of a MAJ n−4 ◦MAJ  n  n−4 circuit computing MAJn is equivalent to the existence of an ((n − 4, n), (4, 3), n−4 2 , 2 + 1) list expander. Moreover, an explicit construction of such a circuit implies an explicit construction of such an expander, and vice versa. Currently, we do not know whether such an expander can be built from known constructions of expanders in the usual sense. A similar argument to the proof of Theorem 4 can show that a list expander of the form “d1 choose d2 ” for d2 > d1 /2 + 1 captures a promise version of the problem for constructing majority circuits. The proof of Theorem 6 is very similar to the proof of Theorem 4 and omitted in this version.
context: Note that our definition of an expander is different from the usual definition in a sense that the expansion property is only required for the sets of size equal to K. Let C be a MAJn−c ◦ MAJn−c circuit over {x1 , . . . , xn } and let GC be a c-leftregular bipartite graph associated to C. Suppose that d is an integer such that d ≥ 2c + 1. Then, the following are equivalent. (i) C(x) = 1 for every |x| = b n2 c − 2c + d and C(x) = 0 for every |x| = d n2 e + 2c − d. (ii) GC is an ((n − c, n), (c, d), d n−c n c 2 e, b 2 c − 2 + d) list expander. M FC S 2 0 1 8
